basics.name: Taleef Tamsal
basics.label: Software Developer | LLM Safety and Evaluation Researcher
basics.summary: Software developer and researcher working on LLM safety and adversarial robustness, reliable evaluation, agentic AI security, and trustworthy NLP/RAG. First author of an AACL-IJCNLP 2026 Findings paper, a NeurIPS 2026 workshop oral, and two SemEval 2026 system papers; sole developer of a production FHIR/CQL quality-measure platform.

work.name: Medical Informatics Engineering
work.summary: Building WorkWell Measure Studio as its sole developer: a TypeScript/Next.js platform that runs CMS FHIR/CQL measure logic, reads FHIR R4 data through SMART Backend Services, and keeps the evidence behind each computed result.
highlights: Made measure correctness a release gate: nine CMS measures pass all 455 official MADiE test cases.
Backend covered by 3,268 automated tests; a read-only MCP interface exposes 13 role-gated tools without allowing AI to determine compliance.

work.name: Purdue University Fort Wayne
work.position: Graduate Researcher, LLM Safety and Evaluation (advised by Dr. Jonathan Rusert)
work.summary: Controlled study of how LoRA, QLoRA, 4-bit quantization, and full fine-tuning affect jailbreak robustness across five open-weight LLM families, with six attacks on HarmBench and JailbreakBench and three automated judges checked against 750 blind human annotations.
highlights: Used a pre-specified ±5 pp TOST to show that LoRA and full fine-tuning had equivalent black-box safety degradation under the controlled recipe; QLoRA was more variable, and 4-bit quantization alone showed no meaningful degradation.

Found that evaluator choice could change the conclusion as much as the adaptation method: GPT-4o-mini mislabeled 45.7% of human-consensus safe outputs as jailbreaks (8.6% for HB-Cls), inflating measured degradation by about 3x.
For the JUDGe study, showed that GPT-5.6 judge configurations still over-flagged 21.5–29.9% of safe completions, and identical outputs received different labels on 3–15% of repeat evaluations.
